objectives:
"Objective: This course introduces fundamental concepts of Computer Science/Engineering. In addition, the class will discuss basic programming skills. C and/or C++ language will be taught. The following outline is from the main textbook. This course outline could be changed if time is not allowed to complete all lectures. Additional lectures for term projects and assignments could be added to the outline.

In each week, the class will discuss fundamental concepts for one hour, plus programming skills for two hours. The lab experiment class (i.e., Introduction to Computer Science LabⅠ) will discuss skills to complete assignments and projects."
content:
"The following outline for Computer Science Fundamentals is for both Introduction to Computer Science Ⅰand II (which will be taught in the Spring semester):

1. Introduction
2. Number System
3. Storing Data
4. Operations on Data
5. Computer Organizations
6. Computer Networks
7. Operating Systems
8. Algorithms
9. Programming Languages
10. Software Engineering
11. Data Structure
12. Abstract Data Type
13. File Structure
14. Databases
15. Data Compression
16. Security
17. Theory of Computation
18. Artificial Intelligent

Course Outline for C/C++ Programming

Chapter 2: Introduction to C++ Programming
Chapter 3: Introduction to Classes and Objects
Chapter 4,5: Control Statements
Chapter 6: Functions and an Introduction to Recursion
Chapter 7: Arrays and Vectors
Chapter 8: Pointers
Chapter 9, 10: Classes
Chapter 11: Operator Overloading
Chapter 12: Inheritance
Chapter 13: Polymorphism (optional)
Chapter 14: Templates (optional)
Chapter 16: Exception Handling (optional)

In the Spring semester, Java Programming will be taught."
books: """C++ How to Program"", Seventh Edition, Late Objects Version, Deitel and Deitel, Prentice Hall."
